answer: A falconry licence is a rare, slow identity anchor: the wildlife agency issues one licence per person only after a two-year apprenticeship, a written exam, and a mews inspection. A wander of a thousand fake falconers is impossible because each licence needs two years of a real mentor's time and a live bird of prey. The horizon of the check is the annual inspection: the agency visits the mews, weighs the bird, and re-signs the licence. The signal that exposes forged papers is the national register: a licence number without a named apprentice and mentor is rejected outright.
